mcqs.q: A prerequisite for defining periodontal health is:
mcqs.explain: Health is a state free from inflammatory periodontal disease — absence of inflammation is essential.

mcqs.q: Periodontal health can also be restored on a periodontium that is:
mcqs.explain: Health can be re-established even on an anatomically reduced periodontium (after past disease).

mcqs.q: Which is a determinant of clinical periodontal health?
mcqs.explain: Determinants are microbiological (plaque), host (local + systemic) and environmental (smoking, drugs, stress, nutrition).

mcqs.q: In periodontal health, the probing depth is typically:
mcqs.explain: Healthy probing depths are about 2–3 mm with no bleeding or attachment loss.

mcqs.q: Which finding is INCOMPATIBLE with periodontal health?
mcqs.explain: Health requires no bleeding on probing and no colour/contour/consistency change.

mcqs.q: Gingivitis is best described as an inflammatory lesion that:
opts: Stays contained within the gingiva (no attachment loss)
mcqs.explain: Plaque-induced gingivitis is contained within the gingiva and does not involve attachment loss.

mcqs.q: A key feature of gingivitis (vs periodontitis) is that it is:
mcqs.explain: Gingivitis is reversible once plaque is controlled.

mcqs.q: The primary parameter for diagnosing gingivitis is:
mcqs.explain: BOP is the primary diagnostic parameter for plaque-induced gingivitis.

mcqs.q: Plaque-induced gingivitis is divided into how many categories?
mcqs.explain: Three: biofilm alone; mediated by systemic/local risk factors; drug-influenced enlargement.

mcqs.q: A classic systemic risk factor that modifies plaque-induced gingivitis is:
mcqs.explain: Pregnancy is a systemic modifier (pregnancy gingivitis); plaque-retentive factors are local modifiers.

mcqs.q: Which trio of drugs classically causes gingival enlargement?
mcqs.explain: Phenytoin (anticonvulsant), nifedipine (calcium-channel blocker) and cyclosporine (immunosuppressant) cause gingival overgrowth.

mcqs.q: Drug-induced gingival enlargement is predominantly:
opts: Interproximal and nodular, covering 1/3–1/2 of the crowns
mcqs.explain: It is predominantly interproximal, nodular overgrowth covering one-third to one-half of the crowns, especially anteriorly.

mcqs.q: Non-plaque-induced gingival lesions characteristically:
opts: Do NOT resolve after plaque removal
mcqs.explain: They are not caused by plaque and do not resolve with plaque removal, though severity may worsen with plaque.

mcqs.q: Herpetic gingival lesions typically present as:
opts: Intraoral blisters that burst into tiny ulcers
mcqs.explain: Viral (herpetic) lesions are intraoral vesicles that quickly rupture into small ulcerations.

mcqs.q: An 'aspirin burn' of the gingiva is an example of a:
mcqs.explain: Chemical injury (e.g. aspirin held against mucosa) is a traumatic non-plaque gingival lesion.

mcqs.q: According to the 2017 classification, the three forms of periodontitis are necrotizing periodontitis, periodontitis, and:
opts: Periodontitis as a manifestation of systemic disease
mcqs.explain: The three forms are necrotizing periodontitis, periodontitis, and periodontitis as a direct manifestation of systemic disease.

mcqs.q: A hallmark intraoral finding of necrotizing periodontitis is:
mcqs.explain: Punched-out, crater-like interdental ulcerations with necrosis and a pseudomembrane are characteristic.

mcqs.q: Which predisposing factors are classically linked to necrotizing periodontitis?
mcqs.explain: The typical case is a stressed heavy smoker with poor oral hygiene, pain, bleeding and fetid breath.

mcqs.q: The whitish film covering the attached gingiva in necrotizing disease is a:
mcqs.explain: A thin whitish pseudomembrane covers the affected gingiva in necrotizing periodontitis.

mcqs.q: Papillon-Lefèvre syndrome is inherited as:
mcqs.explain: PLS is an autosomal-recessive disorder.

mcqs.q: The extra-oral hallmark of Papillon-Lefèvre syndrome is:
mcqs.explain: PLS combines severe periodontitis with hyperkeratosis of the palms, soles and knees.

mcqs.q: Papillon-Lefèvre syndrome affects:
mcqs.explain: PLS affects both dentitions, with mobility and abscesses soon after tooth eruption.

mcqs.q: A recognised distribution pattern of periodontitis is:
mcqs.explain: A molar-incisor distribution pattern of periodontitis is recognised in the 2017 framework.

mcqs.q: In gingivitis, attachment level and alveolar bone are:
mcqs.explain: Gingivitis shows no attachment loss and no radiographic bone loss — both are preserved.

mcqs.q: Pregnancy gingivitis is an example of plaque-induced gingivitis that is:
opts: Mediated by a systemic risk factor
mcqs.explain: Hormonal changes in pregnancy act as a systemic modifier of plaque-induced gingivitis.

mcqs.q: Necrotizing periodontitis commonly produces which extra-oral sign?
mcqs.explain: Tender submandibular nodes, fever and malaise can accompany necrotizing periodontitis.

mcqs.q: Which statement about gingival health on a reduced periodontium is correct?
opts: Health can exist with reduced bone but no inflammation
mcqs.explain: After successful treatment, health (no inflammation, no BOP) can exist on an anatomically reduced periodontium.

mcqs.q: Identify the gingival condition shown — nodular overgrowth in a patient on a calcium-channel blocker.
mcqs.explain: Nodular interproximal gingival overgrowth from phenytoin/nifedipine/cyclosporine is drug-induced enlargement.

mcqs.q: Identify these intraoral vesicles/ulcers of viral origin.
mcqs.explain: Intraoral blisters that burst into small ulcers are herpetic (viral) gingival lesions — a non-plaque lesion.

mcqs.q: Identify the gingival presentation with punched-out craters in a stressed smoker.
mcqs.explain: Necrosis with punched-out interdental craters and a pseudomembrane indicates necrotizing periodontitis.

mcqs.q: These keratotic palms/soles in a child with severe periodontitis suggest:
mcqs.explain: Palmoplantar hyperkeratosis with severe early periodontitis is Papillon-Lefèvre syndrome.

saqs.q: Define periodontal health and give two clinical criteria.
saqs.a: A state free from inflammatory periodontal disease. Criteria: no bleeding on probing, probing depth 2–3 mm, no attachment/bone loss, no colour/contour change.

saqs.q: Why is bleeding on probing important in gingivitis?
saqs.a: It is the primary diagnostic parameter of plaque-induced gingivitis and an early objective sign of inflammation.

saqs.q: Name the three drugs that classically cause gingival enlargement.
List the three forms of periodontitis in the 2017 classification.
saqs.a: Necrotizing periodontitis; periodontitis; periodontitis as a direct manifestation of systemic disease.

saqs.q: Give three clinical features of necrotizing periodontitis.
saqs.a: Punched-out interdental craters/ulcers, whitish pseudomembrane, pain, fetid breath/halitosis, bleeding (smoker + stress).

saqs.q: What is Papillon-Lefèvre syndrome and its inheritance?
saqs.a: An autosomal-recessive disorder with severe periodontitis (both dentitions) plus palmoplantar hyperkeratosis.
